You are an AI assistant specialized in building rapid prototypes in Google AI Studio. Your task is to generate a Signage Lab Platform v0 suitable for mobile and experimentation. Requirements: 1. Modules & Architecture - Media Library Module: - Table with metadata: mediaId, name, type, duration, tags, preview URL - Upload form that stores files in cloud storage (GCS/S3) and metadata in tables - Playlist Builder Module: - Form to select media and assign template - Store playlists as JSON in table - Templates Module: - Table for HTML/CSS/JS snippets - Preview iframe for template inspection - Device Registry Module: - Table for devices: playerId, platform, capabilities, last seen - Debug / Inspector Module: - Embed existing tools (meta video inspector, playlist generator, remote debug) via iframe or API - Action Buttons / Automation: - Provision players (generate JSON config for JS player) - Send remote debug commands Storage: - Use Google Cloud Storage for media files - Use AI Studio Tables for metadata, playlists, templates, devices - Keep large assets separate to avoid UI lag 2. Workflow - Step 1: Upload media → metadata stored in tables - Step 2: Create playlist → select media + assign template → store as JSON - Step 3: Manage templates → add HTML/CSS/JS snippets → assign templateId to playlist - Step 4: Register device → assign playerId, platform, capabilities - Step 5: Generate player config → combine device info + playlist + template into JSON → store in PlayerConfigs table - Step 6: Player consumption → JS player fetches JSON config, loads playlist, applies template, connects to debug endpoint 3. Player JSON Config Template - Include fields: playerId, device info (platform, model, capabilities), playlist (items with mediaId, type, URL, duration, templateId), template snippets (HTML, CSS, JS), debug endpoint, lastProvisioned timestamp - Example JSON: { "playerId": "player-001", "device": { "platform": "webos", "model": "LG 55XE3C", "capabilities": {"videoCodec":["h264","hevc"],"webgl":true,"maxResolution":"4k"} }, "playlist": { "id": "playlist-001", "name": "Morning Loop", "items": [ {"mediaId":"media-001","type":"video","url":"https://storage.googleapis.com/.../video1.mp4","duration":30}, {"mediaId":"media-002","type":"image","url":"https://storage.googleapis.com/.../image1.png","duration":10} ], "templateId": "template-001" }, "template": { "id":"template-001","name":"Standard Fullscreen", "htmlSnippet":"
", "cssSnippet":"body{margin:0; background:black;}", "jsSnippet":"console.log('Template loaded');" }, "debug":{"enabled":true,"wsEndpoint":"wss://my-signage-debug-endpoint.example.com"}, "lastProvisioned":"2025-12-28T12:00:00Z" } 4. AI Studio Tables Example - Media Table: mediaId, name, type, url, duration, tags - Playlist Table: playlistId, name, mediaIds[], templateId - Template Table: templateId, name, htmlSnippet, cssSnippet, jsSnippet - Device Table: playerId, platform, model, capabilities - PlayerConfigs Table: playerId, configJSON, lastProvisioned 5. Mobile-First UX Considerations - Quick swipe/navigation between modules (media, playlist, templates, devices) - One-click JSON config generation - Lightweight player fetch API for mobile networks - Toggleable debug panel modal - Playlist preview and template iframe preview 6. Output Requirements - Step-by-step AI Studio scaffolding instructions - Table definitions, forms, and actions - Instructions for embedding external tools - Example player JSON provisioning The goal is to produce a fully functional v0 platform for experimentation where media can be uploaded, templates assigned, playlists created, players provisioned, and experimental tools embedded, all with a mobile-first experience.

**Designing the Signage Platform**

I've been conceptualizing the core modules for this React application. We're prioritizing mobile responsiveness and flexibility.  The media library is forming with a table view and upload functionality.  I'm also working on playlist and template modules, which I envision as a JSON-based playlist with a simple template previewing system using snippets.


**Building the Architecture**

I'm now deep-diving into the app's structure. I've defined key data structures for media, playlists, templates, and devices. Core modules are emerging, focusing on a responsive UI using Tailwind, Lucide icons, and React 18. I'm focusing on structuring a robust services layer, abstracting the storage logic, and planning on using local storage to simulate "AI Studio Tables." I'm also considering a mobile-friendly navigation design using a bottom tab bar or sidebar.


**Structuring the UI Components**

I'm presently building out the UI components, focusing on card-based views and modals for adding/editing data. I'm also including JSON previews for configurations. For data persistence, a `MockDB` service using `localStorage` will simulate an AI Studio table environment. Media uploads are mocked using `picsum.photos` URLs and local data URLs. I'm also considering a "Sync" button to prepare the data in the requested JSON format. I plan to incorporate a setup guide, or table view within the app, to explain the underlying structure, since the focus is a functional React app.


**Implementing New Features**

I'm now integrating new components, specifically `TemplatesManager`, `DeviceRegistry`, `DebugInspector`, and `ProvisioningView`.  The approach involves customizable placeholders for embedded tools and I'm ensuring the "Provision" button generates the precise nested structure for the "Player JSON Config Template".

JSON Schema 2.1 PlayerConfig interface PlayerConfig { playerId: string; device: DeviceInfo; playlist: Playlist; template: Template; debug: DebugConfig; lastProvisioned: string; } interface DeviceInfo { platform: "webos" | "tizen" | "android" | "chromium"; model: string; capabilities: { videoCodec: string[]; webgl: boolean; maxResolution?: string; [key: string]: any; }; } interface DebugConfig { enabled: boolean; wsEndpoint: string; } 2.2 Playlist interface Playlist { id: string; name: string; items: PlaylistItem[]; } interface PlaylistItem { mediaId: string; type: "video" | "image" | "audio" | "html"; url: string; duration?: number; // seconds for image/audio startTime?: string; // optional scheduling endTime?: string; transition?: "fade" | "slide" | "none"; templateOverrideId?: string; } 2.3 Template interface Template { id: string; name: string; htmlSnippet: string; // placeholder bindings {{media.url}}, {{playlist.name}} cssSnippet: string; jsSnippet: string; hooks?: { onLoad?: string; onMediaStart?: string; onMediaEnd?: string; } } ⸻ 3. Event Hooks & Telemetry Event Description Payload Example playerInit Player initialized {playerId, timestamp} mediaStart Media item started {mediaId, playlistId, timestamp} mediaEnd Media item ended {mediaId, playlistId, duration} playlistEnd Playlist completed {playlistId, loopCount} error Any playback / asset error {mediaId?, errorCode, message} templateLoad Template applied {templateId, timestamp} debugMessage Custom debug logs {level, message, context} These events can be sent via WebSocket or batched to a telemetry endpoint. ⸻ 4. Asset Preloading & Caching Strategy • Preload next 2-3 playlist items to ensure smooth transitions • Use HTMLVideoElement preload + cache in memory • For images, use Image() objects with onload handlers • Audio: prefetch and decode before playback • Fallback: if asset fails → skip and log error • Optional low-res fallback for network/CPU constrained devices ⸻ 5. Template Engine & Bindings • Support placeholders: • {{media.url}} → current media URL • {{playlist.name}} → playlist name • {{timestamp}} → current ISO time • {{playerId}} → current player ID • Hooks: • onLoad → run custom JS when template is loaded • onMediaStart → run JS at start of each media item • onMediaEnd → run JS at end of media item • Safe execution: • Optionally sandbox JS snippets with Function constructor or iframe isolation ⸻ 6. Mobile / Multi-Platform Considerations • Detect platform via DeviceAdapter → adjust codecs / resolutions • Optimize video preloading for mobile networks • Minimal DOM updates → only update

payload.text: SignageLab Dashboard: This mobile-first dashboard provides a clean overview of system status, recent media updates, and active playlists, all within a modern corporate minimalistic design featuring a white background, black elements, subtle "Google Glass" effects, and a vibrant accent color. payload.text:
Great — thanks for the detailed status. Based on your summary, here’s a structured assessment and next steps to transition the Signage Lab Platform from prototype/mockup to a functional engine while keeping it modular for integration with the TypeScript player applet.

⸻

1. Status Overview

Feature	Current Status	Notes / Next Steps
Media Management	Partial (CRUD with LocalStorage)	Need to store createdAt, support filtering, integrate metadata from real media storage (e.g., GCS).
System Status	Mocked	Replace static counts with dynamic calculations based on real Device.lastSeen timestamps.
Recent Updates	Mocked	Implement dynamic time-ago labels using createdAt and updatedAt timestamps.
Active Playlists	Mocked	Pull actual provisioned PlayerConfigs and link playlists to devices.
Device Registry	Real (mock objects, always online)	Implement real status calculation (Online/Attention/Offline) and add remove/decommission functionality.
Debug Tools	Mocked	Connect Debug Inspector to telemetry stored by the TypeScript Virtual Player; enable real tool integration and remote CLI execution.


⸻

2. Recommended Updates / Roadmap

2.1 Dynamic Device Status
	•	Calculate device status based on lastSeen:

const now = Date.now();
const status = (lastSeen: number) => {
  const diff = now - lastSeen;
  if (diff < 60_000) return "Online";
  if (diff < 5 * 60_000) return "Attention";
  return "Offline";
}


	•	Update dashboard counts dynamically: Online / Attention / Offline.

⸻

2.2 Time-Relative Metadata
	•	Add createdAt / updatedAt to Media and Playlists.
	•	Replace hardcoded "2h ago" with a dynamic time-ago function:

function timeAgo(timestamp: number) {
  const seconds = Math.floor((Date.now() - timestamp) / 1000);
  if (seconds < 60) return `${seconds}s ago`;
  if (seconds < 3600) return `${Math.floor(seconds/60)}m ago`;
  if (seconds < 86400) return `${Math.floor(seconds/3600)}h ago`;
  return `${Math.floor(seconds/86400)}d ago`;
}



⸻

2.3 Real Active Playlists
	•	Pull active playlists from PlayerConfigs table:
	•	If a device has a provisioned config → display as active playlist.
	•	Update the dashboard to reflect which media is playing per device.

⸻

2.4 Device Management
	•	Add functionality for:
	•	Removing / decommissioning devices
	•	Editing device metadata (platform, model, capabilities)
	•	Ensure dashboard updates dynamically after device changes.

⸻

2.5 Enhanced Telemetry Integration
	•	Link the Debug Inspector to real telemetry:
	•	Virtual Player emits events (mediaStart, mediaEnd, templateLoad, errors) to localStorage or WebSocket.
	•	Dashboard fetches and displays telemetry per device.
	•	Debug tool buttons trigger live inspection or replay of telemetry logs.

⸻

2.6 Additional Improvements
	•	Filtering & Search: Add filters for media type, tags, playlists, devices.
	•	Real-time Updates: Use polling or WebSocket to update device status, active playlists, and recent updates dynamically.
	•	UI Consistency: Ensure the carousel, progress bars, and “Playing” statuses reflect real-time player activity.

⸻

3. Integration with TypeScript Player Applet
	•	The PlayerConfig JSON will now drive real active playlists.
	•	Telemetry emitted by the player will feed the Debug Inspector module.
	•	Devices marked as online/offline in the dashboard should correspond to actual connectivity and last-seen timestamps from player telemetry.
	•	All provisioning actions (create playlist, assign template) will generate JSON the TypeScript player applet can consume.

⸻

Next Recommended Steps
	1.	Implement dynamic device status and time-relative metadata first; this is foundational.
	2.	Connect real active playlists to the dashboard using provisioned PlayerConfigs.
	3.	Update Debug Inspector to consume telemetry from virtual or real players.
	4.	Enhance device management and UI consistency.
	5.	Begin integration tests with the TypeScript player applet: ensure JSON configs from dashboard correctly drive the player.

⸻

**Reviewing the Platform**

I'm currently focused on the Signage Lab Platform v0. The Media Library's search and filtering capabilities are working well. I'm now looking closely at the Templates Manager to assess its current state and functionality.

My immediate focus is implementing dynamic progress bars on the dashboard using either telemetry data or simulation. I'm also transitioning the virtual player to an iframe for genuine template rendering. Additionally, I'm working to connect the "Remote Inspect" feature in the device registry to the debug view, and implementing command simulation within the debug inspector. I'm also improving some minor UI details in provisioning.


**Making Deployments Dynamic**

My plan is to make the progress bars and display names dynamically reflect real-time data from the `PlayerConfig` and `Telemetry`.
